headline: Bullish on Perth apartment market: Garden Towers 82% sold at $210M, settlements beginning within 14 days contributing to H1 FY revenue, with $2B five-year pipeline and imminent launches
reasoning: Finbar has completed its Garden Towers development in East Perth comprising 342 lots, with 82% sold equating to approximately $210M in presale contracts. Settlements are expected to begin within 14 days, with all revenue falling into the first half of the current financial year and the remaining stock expected to sell within 6-12 months. The company sees structural undersupply in Perth apartments, minimal rental vacancy, and a lack of competing projects or cranes on the horizon. The five-year development pipeline amounts to close to $2 billion with new launches imminent. Recent Parkside project launch saw 27 apartments sold on launch day, with investors making up 75% of buyers and 50% being repeat purchasers, indicating strong demand from both investor and owner-occupier segments.
quote: Look, this, this project is certainly a project that has been in the milestone since we launched or started construction back in 2024. You know, it's gone through the period of COVID with a shortage of undersupply and labour. But certainly this project represents a good milestone in terms of our resilience into the market. The the whole revenue will fall into this financial year, first half of financial year with the balance of stock to be sold within the next 6 to 12 months.
episode_title: Finbar banks $210M in sales as Perth apartments run short

headline: Perth apartment market in structural undersupply: vacancy rates at lows, renters transitioning to ownership, investors chasing high yields, and no new competing supply visible
reasoning: Ronald Chan highlights a fundamental undersupply of apartments in Perth, with vacancy rates at minimal levels and virtually no rental availability. This is driving renters to transition to owner-occupation and attracting investors seeking high yields. Critically, Garden Towers is described as the only project completing in the near term with no new projects or cranes visible on the horizon, creating an extremely tight market. This competitive vacuum underpins confidence in the Perth apartment outlook across mid-size price points targeting both investors and first home buyers.
quote: Like I say, there's a under supply in in apartments. Certainly the, the vacancy rates are lowest rental, that's minimal rentals availability in the marketplace. So certainly we see that transition from renters coming to own occupies as well as investors coming into secure apartments because of the high yields that we're achieving. But the, the key, the keynote to make is that there's a lack of competition in the marketplace. Our garden towers project is, is the only project that will be completing. There's certainly no new projects or any cranes in the horizon. So it's a very, very tight market here in Perth.
episode_title: Finbar banks $210M in sales as Perth apartments run short

headline: Finbar acquires new Perth site with estimated end value of $150m, expecting a 2.5 to 3-year turnaround given proximity to completed Bel Air project and low local competition
reasoning: Chan described a new site acquisition located 250 metres west of Finbar's recently completed and successful Bel Air Apartments (196 units). The site is in a council area that is pro-development, reducing planning risk, with the planning process estimated at about six months and construction at 18 months. Chan expects quicker turnaround for this site relative to typical projects, making it attractive for Finbar's delivery model.
quote: This particular site is only 250m west of our recently completed Bel Air Apartments. That's, uh, Bel Air comprises of 196 units, uh, which has been very successful to us. Uh, there's a lack of, uh, competition in the immediate area. It's in a location where the councils are pro-development. So, uh, we feel a site acquisition like this will deliver a quicker turnaround for us. Uh, it's three months in, um, in planning, uh, since the site when we acquired the site. It's another six months to obtain development approval. We'll bring it to market, and then it's a quick, uh, delivery in construction of about 18 months. So a site like this can turn around in about two and a half to three years.
episode_title: Finbar finds room to build on Perth’s apartment boom

headline: Perth dwelling values up 18.5% annually but Chan expects growth to moderate to 5-6% per year, improving affordability for mid-market apartment product
reasoning: Chan acknowledges Perth has been leading the national market in dwelling value growth at 18.5% year-on-year but expects this to stabilise and moderate to around 5-6% per annum going forward. He views stabilisation as a positive development, as it improves affordability for Finbar's mid-tier product, which targets the broader 80% of the market including first home buyers. He notes construction cost inflation has also stabilised.
quote: I think the market's going to probably stabilize and probably increase maybe 5 to 6% year going forward, which is a good thing because it just means affordability for the type of product that we're going to deliver is more catered towards the general market. I mean, I like to see our product, uh, you know, being snapped up by first home buyers and the general market, which comprises of 80%, uh, which very few competitors can work in our space.
episode_title: Finbar finds room to build on Perth’s apartment boom

headline: Proposed negative gearing and CGT changes seen as positive for new apartment demand, as concessions would be limited to new builds and draw investors back to Finbar's product
reasoning: Chan views the proposed federal government changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax as a net positive for Finbar's business, as the concessions are expected to apply specifically to new builds. This should funnel investor demand toward new apartment product such as Finbar's. He notes that investors currently represent 30-40% of Finbar's buyers and the company sees 50% as the appropriate level, suggesting upside to investor demand once policy is confirmed.
quote: I can only see this as positive. It's catering to its new builds. So investors will certainly just lean more towards our product offering. Um, once, once this is set in stone by government, I think we'll see that investor profile come up again, too. At the moment, we're sitting at about 40%, 30 to 40% investor. Our general view is that 50% is what it should be.
episode_title: Finbar finds room to build on Perth’s apartment boom
